about.title: Danville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Contra Costa County recorded one traffic death in the latest full crash year, but for a Danville family that single loss reshapes everything. Wrongful death claims exist to help surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children pursue accountability when a preventable collision takes a loved one's life. California law also allows certain other dependents or heirs to bring a claim if there is no surviving spouse or child. These cases run separately from any criminal proceedings and focus on the financial and emotional toll left behind. In Danville, fatal and serious crashes often trace back to the same corridors that carry heavy commuter traffic — I-680 in both directions and Camino Tassajara among them. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a fee; we simply help connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can review the details, explain the filing deadline, and talk through what recovery may look like for funeral costs, lost income, and the loss of companionship. There's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Decide

items.title: Who Can File Matters
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible only if none of those survive. An attorney can clarify where your family stands before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, though claims against a government entity — such as one involving a county road — carry a much shorter deadline. Missing it can close the door on recovery entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral costs and lost financial support, but also the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a loved one provided. An independent attorney can help account for both the tangible and intangible losses.

items.question: Does it matter that the fatal crash happened on I-680, a state highway?
items.answer: It can affect who is liable and what evidence is available, since state highways involve different maintenance and reporting standards than local roads. An attorney can review the specifics of where on I-680 or Camino Tassajara the crash occurred and what that means for your claim.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of death, but if a government entity is involved the window is much shorter and requires an early notice of claim. It's worth speaking with an attorney soon after a loss to avoid missing any deadline.

items.question: What if our family doesn't include a surviving spouse or children?
items.answer: California law allows certain other dependents or heirs to bring a claim when there's no surviving spouse, domestic partner, or child. An attorney can look at your family's specific situation and explain whether you may have standing to file.
